subject: RStan plot error: Error in list2env(members, envir = e)

messages.author: 10b6c1275697355b
messages.subject: RStan plot error: Error in list2env(members, envir = e)
parts:
Hi there,

I'm trying to follow the Eight Schools example at

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started

but I don't seem to get plot(fit) to work. I get an error message:

> plot(fit)
'pars' not specified. Showing first 10 parameters by default.
ci_level: 0.8 (80% intervals)
outer_level: 0.95 (95% intervals)
Error in list2env(members, envir = e) : 
  names(x) must be a character vector of the same length as x


See attached log of the whole session. I'm running R on a MacBook Air (OSX 10.9.5). Any ideas what is going wrong?

Many thanks
Heather

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: RStan plot error: Error in list2env(members, envir = e)
parts:
It looks like you're getting all sorts of weird warnings/errors (about dependencies not available, non-existent files or directories, something about metadata for class "C++Object", and various other things), most of them not related to the plotting functions. So it's a bit hard to tell from that file what's going on. What happens if you start a fresh R session and run the code below? 

library(rstan)
fit <- stan_demo("eight_schools")
plot(fit)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStan plot error: Error in list2env(members, envir = e)
parts:
On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 1:12:52 PM UTC-5, heather....@gmail.com wrote:
Error in list2env(members, envir = e) : 
  names(x) must be a character vector of the same length as x


See attached log of the whole session. I'm running R on a MacBook Air (OSX 10.9.5). Any ideas what is going wrong?

That one comes from ggplot2, whose new version doesn't work with R 3.1.1. I remember having to hack the ggplot2 source to get around that for older versions of R.

I would upgrade R to the latest version, but mostly for non-RStan reasons.

Ben

Best wishes
Heather

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: RStan plot error: Error in list2env(members, envir = e)
parts:
On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 3:27:49 PM UTC-5, Heather Cordell wrote:
Thanks. I upgraded to the latest version of R and it now works nicely. Might be worth updating the RStan GitHub page where it says "R version 3.0.2 or later is required" since that does not seem to be quite correct (at least, not for doing the plots)...

For an individual with administrative rights to a personal computer, there is really no reason to not be using the latest version of R. But there are people who want to use Stan on remote servers where they do not have administrative rights and the support contract that the server has does not allow upgrading. So, we try to keep Stan working with older versions of R and older compilers, but we don't test them much and so it is not surprising when some things are broken.

Ben

On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 3:55:42 PM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
I’m with Heather here — when I do workshops people follow the
instructions to the letter, and I assume that the requirements are
sufficient (and, for example, don’t bother updating R unless
necessary).  Consequently problems like this are incredibly frustrating.
If older versions work for anything but plotting then that should be
noted as such in the requirements.

We can put whatever we want on the wiki but the DESCRIPTION file is more limiting. The package will refuse to install with versions of R that are earlier than what is listed, which is currently 3.0.2. For conferences, we need to be insisting that people come in with the latest version of R because that is the only thing that is adequately tested.

Ben
